title: Al-A'la: the one who purifies
hook: successful is the one who purifies, remembers and prays, though you prefer this life (87:14–17)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Al-A'la, the Most High, and the words said with a forehead on the floor. Your line was glory to the most high. Did you feel the good kind of small? Day two hundred two.

Here's an experiment psychologists love. Offer someone one cookie now, or two in fifteen minutes. Children squirm, cover their eyes, sing to themselves, lick the cookie. Adults do the same thing with money, sleep, and phones, just less visibly. Now is loud. Later is quiet. Al-A'la names that exact pull, fourteen centuries before the cookie. It first says who succeeds, and then, with a kind of honesty that's almost tender, admits what people actually prefer. Today: the one who purifies.
screen: `ONE COOKIE NOW, OR TWO LATER?` → `NOW IS LOUD. LATER IS QUIET.` → `THE ONE WHO PURIFIES.`

segments.voice: Verse fourteen: successful is the one who purifies himself. The verb is tazakka, from z-k-y, the root we met ten days ago in Ash-Shams, successful is the one who purifies the soul. The same root as zakat: to cleanse, and to grow. Verse fifteen adds two more: he remembers the name of his Lord, and he prays. Purify, remember, pray. Three verbs, and that's the whole description of success. Then verse sixteen turns to the listener, and doesn't scold. It just says: but you prefer the life of this world. It's true, and the surah knows it's true. Now is loud. Then verse seventeen, in Pickthall's words: "Although the Hereafter is better and more lasting." The key word is abqa, more lasting, from a root meaning to remain. It doesn't say this world is worthless. It says the later lasts longer. And verses eighteen and nineteen add a surprise: this is in the earlier scrolls, the scrolls of Ibrahim and Musa. The surah says it isn't saying anything new. Abraham and Moses were told the same. That closes a long stretch of the path. Since day one hundred seventy-seven we've walked backward through the middle of the thirtieth part: the earthquake that reports, the clear proof, the Night of Power, the first word, read. The fig and the olive, the opened chest, the morning, the night, the sun and the soul, the steep path, the dawn, the overwhelming, and the Most High. Tomorrow we begin the opening surahs of the juz', the ones that come first in the book.
screen: `PURIFY, REMEMBER, PRAY.` · `BUT YOU PREFER THIS WORLD.` · `ABQA — MORE LASTING.` · `IN THE SCROLLS OF IBRAHIM AND MUSA.` · then, large: `THE LATER LASTS.`

segments.voice: For two minutes, think about today's choices ahead of you: what you'll eat, what you'll watch, how you'll spend the evening, what you'll say to someone. Find one place where now and later pull in different directions. Don't solve every one. Just pick one, and decide now which way it goes. The bell holds the time.
Al-A'la. The Most High, Surah eighty-seven: success is purifying, remembering, praying, and what comes later is more lasting. Today's word.
Your line: the later lasts. When the loud thing and the lasting thing pull at you today, choose what lasts, once. Day two hundred two.

howItsDone: Muslims often recite Al-A'la in the Friday, Eid and witr prayers; its verses on the one who purifies himself and on the Hereafter being more lasting are widely quoted in sermons and reminders.

match.prompt: what's inside the verses — tap the pairs.
pairs: purified himself, same root as zakat

myth: Al-A'la says this world is worthless
it says the Hereafter is better and more lasting, not that this world counts for nothing.
the surah says its message was already in the scrolls of Ibrahim and Musa
87:18–19: this is in the earlier scrolls.
tazakka shares a root with zakat
z-k-y: to purify and to grow, as in Ash-Shams.

fork.setup: Al-A'la describes the successful person, then turns to the listener. what does it say the listener prefers?
fork.reveal: but you prefer the life of the world, although the Hereafter is better and more lasting (87:16–17). honest, not scolding.

original.note: Arabic: "more lasting," from b-q-y, to remain; the Hereafter is khayrun wa abqa, better and more lasting (87:17).

trapdoor: what you thought: be good now, get rewarded later.
what it means: success is purifying, remembering and praying; people lean toward now, but the later is more lasting.

what a scholar hears: tazakka echoes zakkaha in 91:9; al-baqi, the Everlasting, is among the divine names from the same root b-q-y; 87:18–19 is one of the few Qur'anic mentions of the scrolls of Ibrahim.

sources.quoted: Although the Hereafter is better and more lasting.

sources.ref: Qur'an 87:14–16, 87:18–19 (purify, remember, pray; you prefer this world; the scrolls of Ibrahim and Musa)
Qur'an 91:9 (the same root in Ash-Shams); 53:36–37 (the scrolls of Musa and Ibrahim)
